landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.fact: Built in just 410 days in 1930-31.
landmarks.about: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. The building was designed in the Art Deco style by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon and constructed between 1930 and 1931.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.fact: Named for The New York Times, which moved here in 1904.
landmarks.about: Times Square is one of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections, tourist destinations, and entertainment hubs. It is formed by the junction of Broadway, Seventh Avenue, and 42nd Street in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.

landmarks.name: Grand Central Terminal
landmarks.fact: Its ceiling shows the zodiac painted backwards.
landmarks.about: Grand Central Terminal (GCT; also referred to as Grand Central Station or simply as Grand Central) is a commuter rail terminal at 42nd Street and Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.
landmarks.credit: Fcb981 ; Eric Baetscher (attribution required) CC BY-SA 3.0

landmarks.name: Rockefeller Center
landmarks.fact: Its Christmas tree tradition began in 1931.
landmarks.about: Rockefeller Center is a complex of 19 commercial buildings covering 22 acres (8.9 ha) between 48th Street and 51st Street in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City.

landmarks.name: Flatiron Building
landmarks.fact: Its triangle shape follows the angle of Broadway.
landmarks.about: The Flatiron Building (originally the Fuller Building) is a 22-story, 307-foot-tall (93.6 m) steel-framed triangular building at 175 Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron District neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. Designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P.

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.fact: Its spire was assembled in secret inside the building.
landmarks.about: The Chrysler Building is a 1,046-foot-tall (319 m), Art Deco skyscraper in the East Midtown neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. Located at the intersection of 42nd Street and Lexington Avenue, it is the tallest steel-framed brick building in the world.

landmarks.name: One World Trade Center
landmarks.fact: It stands 1,776 feet tall, for 1776.
landmarks.about: One World Trade Center, also known as One WTC and the Freedom Tower, is the main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan, New York City.

landmarks.name: Charging Bull
landmarks.fact: Dropped off unannounced by artist Arturo Di Modica in 1989.
landmarks.about: Charging Bull (sometimes referred to as the Bull of Wall Street or the Bowling Green Bull) is a bronze sculpture that stands on Broadway just north of Bowling Green in the Financial District of Manhattan in New York City.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Bridge
landmarks.fact: Opened in 1883, it was the world's first steel-wire suspension bridge.
landmarks.about: The Brooklyn Bridge is a cable-stayed suspension bridge in New York City, spanning the East River between the boroughs of Manhattan and Brooklyn. Opened on May 24, 1883, the Brooklyn Bridge was the first fixed crossing of the East River.

landmarks.name: City Hall
landmarks.fact: The oldest US city hall still used for its original purpose.
landmarks.about: New York City Hall is the seat of New York City government, located at the center of City Hall Park in the Civic Center area of Lower Manhattan, between Broadway, Park Row, and Chambers Street.

landmarks.name: Washington Square Arch
landmarks.fact: Built for the centennial of George Washington's inauguration.
landmarks.about: The Washington Square Arch, officially the Washington Arch, is a marble memorial arch at the Washington Square Park, at Greenwich Village neighborhood of Lower Manhattan, New York City, United States.
landmarks.credit: Nan Palmero from San Antonio, TX, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Union Square
landmarks.fact: Home to the city's best-known farmers market.
landmarks.about: Union Square is a historic intersection and surrounding neighborhood in Manhattan, New York City, United States, located where Broadway and the former Bowery Road – now Park Avenue north of the Square – came together in the early 19th century.

landmarks.name: Madison Square Garden
landmarks.fact: The fourth arena to carry the name, sitting atop Penn Station.
landmarks.about: Madison Square Garden, colloquially known as the Garden or by its initials MSG, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, U.S. The arena is located between Seventh and Eighth avenues, extending from 31st to 33rd streets, atop Pennsylvania Station.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Bethesda Terrace
landmarks.fact: Its Angel of the Waters was the first public statue in NYC by a woman.
landmarks.about: Bethesda Terrace and Fountain are two architectural features overlooking the southern shore of the Lake in New York City's Central Park. The fountain, with its Angel of the Waters statue, is located in the center of the terrace.

landmarks.name: Columbus Circle
landmarks.fact: The point from which all official NYC distances are measured.
landmarks.about: Columbus Circle is a traffic circle and busy road junction in the New York City borough of Manhattan, at the intersection of Eighth Avenue, Broadway, Central Park South (West 59th Street), and Central Park West, at the southwest corner of Central Park.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Center
landmarks.fact: Built on land cleared from the old San Juan Hill neighborhood.
landmarks.about: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts (also simply known as Lincoln Center) is a 16.3-acre (6.6-hectare) complex of buildings in the Lincoln Square neighborhood on the Upper West Side of Manhattan. It has thirty indoor and outdoor facilities and is host to five million visitors annually.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: United Nations Headquarters
landmarks.fact: The site is international territory.
landmarks.about: The headquarters of the United Nations (UN) is on 17 to 18 acres (6.9 to 7.3 ha) of grounds in the Turtle Bay neighborhood of Midtown Manhattan in New York City, United States. It borders First Avenue to the west, 42nd Street to the south, 48th Street to the north, and the East River to the east.

landmarks.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
landmarks.fact: The largest Gothic Revival Catholic cathedral in North America.
landmarks.about: St. Patrick's Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City, United States.

landmarks.name: Apollo Theater
landmarks.fact: Amateur Night has launched careers since 1934.
landmarks.about: The Apollo Theater (formerly the Hurtig & Seamon's New Theatre; also Apollo Theatre or 125th Street Apollo Theatre) is a multi-use theater at 253 West 125th Street in the Harlem neighborhood of Upper Manhattan in New York City.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Low Memorial Library
landmarks.fact: The domed centerpiece of Columbia University.
landmarks.about: The Low Memorial Library (nicknamed Low) is a building at the center of Columbia University's campus in Upper Manhattan, New York City, U.S. The building, located near 116th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam Avenue, was designed by Charles Follen McKim of the firm McKim, Mead & White.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
landmarks.fact: Under construction since 1892 and still unfinished.
landmarks.about: The Cathedral of St. John the Divine (sometimes referred to as St.

landmarks.name: Grant's Tomb
landmarks.fact: The largest mausoleum in North America.
landmarks.about: Grant's Tomb, officially the General Grant National Memorial, is the final resting place of Ulysses S. Grant, the 18th president of the United States, and of his wife Julia.

landmarks.name: Little Red Lighthouse
landmarks.fact: Saved from demolition by a 1942 children's book.
landmarks.about: The Little Red Lighthouse, officially Jeffrey's Hook Light, is a small lighthouse located in Fort Washington Park along the Hudson River in Manhattan, New York City, under the George Washington Bridge.

landmarks.name: George Washington Bridge
landmarks.fact: One of the world's busiest motor-vehicle bridges.
landmarks.about: The George Washington Bridge is a double-decked suspension bridge spanning the Hudson River, connecting Fort Lee in Bergen County, New Jersey, with the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City.

landmarks.name: Hamilton Grange
landmarks.fact: Alexander Hamilton's only home, moved twice.
landmarks.about: Hamilton Grange National Memorial (also known as Hamilton Grange or the Grange) is a historic house museum within St. Nicholas Park in the Hamilton Heights neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, United States.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Morris-Jumel Mansion
landmarks.fact: Manhattan's oldest house, Washington's HQ in 1776.
landmarks.about: The Morris–Jumel Mansion (also known as the Morris House, Mount Morris, Jumel Mansion, and Morris–Jumel Mansion Museum) is an 18th-century historic house museum in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Upper Manhattan in New York City, United States.

landmarks.name: The Vessel
landmarks.fact: A honeycomb of 154 flights of stairs at Hudson Yards.
landmarks.about: Vessel is a 16-story, 150-foot-tall (46 m) structure of connected staircases in the 5-acre (2.0 ha) Hudson Yards Public Square of Hudson Yards in Manhattan, New York City.

landmarks.name: Stonewall Inn
landmarks.fact: The first US national monument to LGBTQ+ rights.
landmarks.about: The Stonewall Inn (also known as Stonewall) is a gay bar and recreational tavern at 53 Christopher Street in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City.

landmarks.name: Williamsburg Bridge
landmarks.fact: It was the longest suspension bridge in the world when it opened in 1903.
landmarks.about: The Williamsburg Bridge is a suspension bridge across the East River in New York City, connecting the Lower East Side of Manhattan with the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn. Originally known as the East River Bridge, the Williamsburg Bridge was completed in 1903.

landmarks.name: Manhattan Bridge Arch
landmarks.fact: Its grand entrance was modeled on the Porte Saint-Denis in Paris.
landmarks.about: The Manhattan Bridge is a suspension bridge that crosses the East River in New York City, connecting Lower Manhattan at Canal Street with Downtown Brooklyn at the Flatbush Avenue Extension. Designed by Leon Moisseiff, the bridge has a total length of 6,855 ft (2,089 m).

landmarks.name: Old St. Patrick's Cathedral
landmarks.fact: The city's first Catholic cathedral, dedicated in 1815.
landmarks.credit: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA CC BY-SA 2.0

landmarks.name: South Street Seaport
landmarks.fact: The old port where the city's shipping trade grew up.
landmarks.about: The South Street Seaport is a historic area and neighborhood in the New York City borough of Manhattan, centered where Fulton Street meets the East River, within the Financial District of Lower Manhattan. The Seaport is a designated historic district.

landmarks.name: Staten Island Ferry Terminal
landmarks.fact: The ferry is free and carries about 45,000 people a day.
landmarks.about: The Whitehall Terminal is a ferry terminal in the South Ferry section of Lower Manhattan, New York City, at the corner of South Street and Whitehall Street. It is used by the Staten Island Ferry, which connects the island boroughs of Manhattan and Staten Island.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Astor Place Cube
landmarks.fact: The 'Alamo' sculpture spins if you push hard enough.
landmarks.about: Alamo, also known as the Astor Place Cube or simply The Cube, is an outdoor sculpture by Tony Rosenthal, located on Astor Place, in the East Village neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It is a black cube, 8 feet (2.4 m) long on each side, mounted on a corner.

landmarks.name: Gramercy Park
landmarks.fact: Manhattan's only private park; residents hold keys.
landmarks.about: Gramercy Park () is the name of both a small, fenced-in private park, and the surrounding neighborhood (which is also referred to as Gramercy), in Manhattan in New York City.

landmarks.name: Gracie Mansion
landmarks.fact: The official residence of the Mayor since 1942.
landmarks.about: Gracie Mansion (also known as Archibald Gracie Mansion) is the official residence of the mayor of New York City. Built in 1799, it is located in Carl Schurz Park, at East End Avenue and 88th Street in the Yorkville neighborhood of Manhattan.

landmarks.name: Roosevelt Island Tramway
landmarks.fact: One of the few commuter aerial tramways in North America.
landmarks.about: The Roosevelt Island Tramway is an aerial tramway that crosses the East River in New York City, connecting Roosevelt Island to the Upper East Side of Manhattan.

landmarks.name: Carnegie Hall
landmarks.fact: Tchaikovsky conducted on opening night in 1891.
landmarks.about: Carnegie Hall ( KAR-nig-ee) is a concert venue at 881 Seventh Avenue, between 56th and 57th Streets, in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Javits Center
landmarks.fact: Its green roof is home to thousands of birds and bees.
landmarks.about: The Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, commonly known as the Javits Center, is a large convention center on Eleventh Avenue between 34th Street and 38th Street in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan, New York City.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: The Dakota
landmarks.fact: Named because it once seemed as remote as the Dakota Territory.
landmarks.about: The Dakota, also known as the Dakota Apartments, is a cooperative apartment building at 1 West 72nd Street on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US.
landmarks.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Dyckman Farmhouse
landmarks.fact: Manhattan's last remaining Dutch colonial farmhouse.
landmarks.about: The Dyckman House, now the Dyckman Farmhouse Museum, is the oldest remaining farmhouse on Manhattan island, a vestige of New York City's rural past.

landmarks.name: Strawberry Fields
landmarks.fact: Its 'Imagine' mosaic honors John Lennon.
landmarks.about: Strawberry Fields is a 2.5-acre (1.0 ha) landscaped section in New York City's Central Park, designed by the landscape architect Bruce Kelly, that is dedicated to the memory of former Beatles member John Lennon. It is named after the Beatles' song "Strawberry Fields Forever", written by Lennon.

landmarks.name: Belvedere Castle
landmarks.fact: A 'folly' built as a lookout, now a weather station.
landmarks.about: Belvedere Castle is a folly in Central Park in Manhattan, New York City. It contains exhibit rooms, an observation deck, and since 1919 has housed Central Park’s official weather station.

landmarks.name: The Plaza Hotel
landmarks.fact: Home of Eloise, the girl who lived on the top floor.
landmarks.about: The Plaza Hotel (also known as The Plaza) is a luxury hotel and condominium apartment building in Midtown Manhattan in New York City.

landmarks.name: Port Authority Bus Terminal
landmarks.fact: The busiest bus terminal in the world.
landmarks.about: The Port Authority Bus Terminal (colloquially known as the Port Authority and by its acronym PABT) is a bus terminal located in Manhattan in New York City.

landmarks.name: Harlem Meer
landmarks.fact: Meer is Dutch for lake.
landmarks.about: Harlem Meer is a man-made lake at the northeast corner of New York City's Central Park. It lies west of Fifth Avenue, south of 110th Street, and north of the Conservatory Garden, near the Harlem and East Harlem neighborhoods of Manhattan.

landmarks.name: Audubon Ballroom
landmarks.fact: Where Malcolm X was assassinated in 1965.
landmarks.about: The Audubon Theatre and Ballroom (generally referred to as the Audubon Ballroom) was a theatre and ballroom located at 3940 Broadway, at the intersection with West 165th Street, in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It was built in 1912 and was designed by Thomas W.

landmarks.name: Shepard Hall
landmarks.fact: City College's Gothic hall, clad in Manhattan schist.

landmarks.name: Ghostbusters Firehouse
landmarks.fact: Hook & Ladder 8 played the Ghostbusters' HQ in 1984.
landmarks.credit: Phillip Ritz; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 00:35, 14 December 2015 (UTC) CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Hotel Chelsea
landmarks.fact: Home over the years to Twain, Warhol, and Patti Smith.
landmarks.about: The Hotel Chelsea (also known as the Chelsea Hotel and the Chelsea) is a hotel at 222 West 23rd Street in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.

landmarks.name: Macy's Herald Square
landmarks.fact: Once billed as the world's largest store.
landmarks.about: Macy's Herald Square (originally named the R. H.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Borough Hall
landmarks.fact: Brooklyn's city hall from when it was its own city, until 1898.
landmarks.about: Brooklyn Borough Hall is a building in Downtown Brooklyn, New York City. It was designed by architects Calvin Pollard and Gamaliel King in the Greek Revival style, and constructed of Tuckahoe marble under the supervision of superintendent Stephen Haynes.

landmarks.name: Barclays Center
landmarks.fact: Its rusted-steel skin is made of 12,000 weathered panels.
landmarks.about: Barclays Center ( BAR-kleez) is a multi-purpose indoor arena in the New York City borough of Brooklyn in the United States. The arena is home to the New York Liberty of the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) and the Brooklyn Nets of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

landmarks.name: Jane's Carousel
landmarks.fact: A 1922 carousel restored over 25 years, now in a glass box by the river.
landmarks.about: Jane's Carousel (formerly Idora Park Merry-Go-Round) is a carved wooden 48-horse carousel in Brooklyn, New York City, built in 1922 by the Philadelphia Toboggan Company (PTC) for the Idora Park amusement park in Youngstown, Ohio.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Heights Promenade
landmarks.fact: It sits on top of a highway, with one of the best views of Manhattan.
landmarks.about: The Brooklyn Heights Promenade, also called the Esplanade, is a 1,826-foot-long (557 m) platform and pedestrian walkway cantilevered over the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (Interstate 278) in Brooklyn Heights, Brooklyn, New York City, United States.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard
landmarks.fact: It built the USS Missouri, where World War II ended.
landmarks.about: The Brooklyn Navy Yard (originally known as the New York Navy Yard) is a shipyard and industrial complex in northwest Brooklyn in New York City, New York, U.S. The Navy Yard is located on the East River in Wallabout Bay, a semicircular bend of the river across from Corlears Hook in Manhattan.

landmarks.name: Domino Park
landmarks.fact: Built on the site of a sugar refinery that once made half of America's sugar.
landmarks.about: Domino Park is a 5-acre (2.0 ha) public park in the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. It spans a quarter mile along the East River near the Williamsburg Bridge, at the Domino Sugar Refinery site.

landmarks.name: Fort Greene Park
landmarks.fact: Its 149-foot column honors over 11,000 prisoners who died on British ships.
landmarks.about: Fort Greene Park is a city-owned and -operated park in Fort Greene, Brooklyn. The 30.2-acre (12.2 ha) park was originally named after the fort formerly located there, Fort Putnam, itself was named for Rufus Putnam, George Washington's chief of engineers in the Revolutionary War.

landmarks.name: Grand Army Plaza
landmarks.fact: Its arch honors Union soldiers of the Civil War.
landmarks.about: Grand Army Plaza, originally known as Prospect Park Plaza, is a public plaza that comprises the northern corner and the main entrance of Prospect Park in the New York City borough of Brooklyn.

landmarks.name: Pratt Institute
landmarks.fact: Its campus doubles as a sculpture park with over 70 works.
landmarks.about: Pratt Institute is a private university with its main campus in Brooklyn, New York. It has an additional campus in Manhattan and an extension campus in Utica, New York at the Munson-Williams-Proctor Arts Institute.

landmarks.name: Williamsburg Bridge (Brooklyn)
landmarks.fact: Its towers were the first bridge towers made entirely of steel.
landmarks.about: The Williamsburg Bridge is a suspension bridge across the East River in New York City, connecting the Lower East Side of Manhattan with the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn. Originally known as the East River Bridge, the Williamsburg Bridge was completed in 1903.

landmarks.name: Gowanus Canal
landmarks.fact: Once one of the most polluted waterways in the US, now a Superfund cleanup.
landmarks.about: The Gowanus Canal (originally known as Gowanus Creek) is a 1.8-mile-long (2.9 km) canal in the New York City borough of Brooklyn, on the westernmost portion of Long Island.

landmarks.name: McCarren Park
landmarks.fact: Its huge 1936 pool sat empty for 28 years before reopening in 2012.
landmarks.about: McCarren Park is a public park in Brooklyn, New York City. It is located on the border of Williamsburg and Greenpoint and is bordered by Nassau Avenue, Bayard Street, Lorimer Street and North 12th Street.

landmarks.name: DUMBO Archway
landmarks.fact: DUMBO stands for Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass.
landmarks.about: Dumbo (or DUMBO, an acronym for Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass) is a neighborhood in the New York City borough of Brooklyn.

landmarks.name: Gantry Plaza State Park
landmarks.fact: Its giant gantries once loaded rail cars onto river barges.
landmarks.about: Gantry Plaza State Park is a 12-acre (4.9 ha) state park on the East River in the Hunters Point section of Long Island City, in the New York City borough of Queens. The park is located in a former dockyard and manufacturing district, and includes remnants of facilities from the area's past.
landmarks.credit: Joe Mabel from Seattle, US CC BY-SA 2.0

landmarks.name: Queensboro Plaza
landmarks.fact: An elevated station where the 7 and N/W trains meet above the streets.
landmarks.about: The Queensboro Plaza station (originally named the Queensboro Bridge Plaza station or simply Bridge Plaza station) is an elevated New York City Subway station at Queens Plaza (originally called Queensboro Bridge Plaza or simply Bridge Plaza) in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens.

landmarks.name: Silvercup Studios
landmarks.fact: An old bread bakery turned TV studio; The Sopranos filmed here.
landmarks.about: Silvercup Studios is a film and television production facility in New York City. The studio is located in Long Island City, Queens, with another facility in the Port Morris neighborhood of the Bronx.

landmarks.name: One Court Square
landmarks.fact: Queens' tallest building for decades, a lone green glass tower.
landmarks.about: One Court Square, also known as the Citicorp Building or the Citigroup Building, is a 50-story, 673-foot (205 m) office tower in Long Island City, Queens, across the East River from Manhattan in New York City, United States.

landmarks.name: Astoria Park
landmarks.fact: Home to NYC's oldest and largest public pool, from 1936.
landmarks.about: Astoria Park is a 59.96-acre (24.26 ha) public park in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City. The park is situated on the eastern shore of the Hell Gate, a strait of the East River, between Ditmars Boulevard to the north and Hoyt Avenue to the south.

landmarks.name: Kaufman Astoria Studios
landmarks.fact: Silent films were shot here in the 1920s; Sesame Street is taped here now.
landmarks.about: The Kaufman Astoria Studios, known historically as the Paramount Studios Complex, is a film studio located in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City. The studio was constructed for Famous Players–Lasky in 1920, since it was close to Manhattan's Theater District.

landmarks.name: Queensbridge Park
landmarks.fact: Sits right under the Queensboro Bridge by the East River.
landmarks.about: Queensbridge Park, named for the nearby Queensboro Bridge, is a 20.34-acre (8.23 ha) city park along the East River in Long Island City, Queens, New York City.

landmarks.name: Steinway Street
landmarks.fact: Named for the piano family whose factory is still in Astoria.
landmarks.about: Steinway Street is a major, 2.4-mile (3.9 km), two-way street in the borough of Queens in New York City, New York, in the United States.

landmarks.name: LaGuardia Community College
landmarks.fact: Housed in a former factory for White Motor Company trucks.
landmarks.about: LaGuardia Community College is a public community college in New York City. It is in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in and part of the City University of New York.

landmarks.name: Hunters Point Library
landmarks.fact: A concrete library with windows carved into odd shapes.

landmarks.name: Yankee Stadium
landmarks.fact: The Yankees have won 27 World Series, more than any other team.
landmarks.about: Yankee Stadium (also referred to as New Yankee Stadium to distinguish it from the original) is a baseball stadium located in the Bronx, New York City. It is the home field of Major League Baseball’s New York Yankees.

landmarks.name: Bronx County Courthouse
landmarks.fact: An Art Deco courthouse wrapped in carved limestone figures.
landmarks.about: The Bronx County Courthouse, also known as the Mario Merola Building, is a historic courthouse building located in the Concourse and Melrose neighborhoods of the Bronx in New York City. It was designed in 1931 and built between 1931 and 1934.

landmarks.name: Andrew Freedman Home
landmarks.fact: Built as a retirement home for millionaires who had lost their fortunes.
landmarks.about: The Andrew Freedman Home is a historic building in the Bronx, New York City. Constructed by the estate of the millionaire Andrew Freedman, it has been renovated into an artists' hub consisting of an interdisciplinary artist residency, an incubator space, workforce development and community services.

landmarks.name: The Hub
landmarks.fact: The Bronx's busiest shopping district, where five streets meet.
landmarks.about: The Hub is a major commercial center for the South Bronx, New York. It is located where four roads converge: East 149th Street, Willis Avenue, Melrose Avenue, and Third Avenues.

landmarks.name: Hostos Community College
landmarks.fact: Named for Eugenio María de Hostos, a Puerto Rican educator.
landmarks.about: Eugenio María de Hostos Community College of The City University of New York is a public community college in the South Bronx, New York City.

landmarks.name: Bronx Terminal Market
landmarks.fact: A 1920s produce market turned shopping center by the river.
landmarks.about: Bronx Terminal Market, also known as Gateway Center at Bronx Terminal Market, is a shopping mall along the Major Deegan Expressway in Concourse, Bronx, New York.

landmarks.name: St. Mary's Park
landmarks.fact: The largest park in the South Bronx, on a rocky hill.
landmarks.about: St. Mary's Park is a public park in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx section of The Bronx, New York City.

landmarks.name: Crotona Park
landmarks.fact: Its lake and pool have served the Bronx since the 1930s.
landmarks.about: Crotona Park is a public park in the South Bronx in New York City, covering 127.5 acres (51.6 ha). The park is bounded by streets of the same name on its northern, eastern, southern, and western borders, and is adjacent to the Crotona Park East and Morrisania neighborhoods of the Bronx.

landmarks.name: Claremont Park
landmarks.fact: Once the estate of the Zborowski family in the 1800s.
landmarks.about: Claremont Park is a park in the Morrisania section of the Bronx in New York City. The land on which the park sits was once part of the Morris family estate and was the site of the Zborowski Mansion.

landmarks.fact: The Staten Island Ferry is free and runs 24 hours a day.

landmarks.name: Staten Island Borough Hall
landmarks.fact: Its clock tower greets every ferry arriving from Manhattan.
landmarks.about: Staten Island Borough Hall is the primary municipal building for the borough of Staten Island in New York City. It is located at 10 Richmond Terrace, next to the Richmond County Courthouse and opposite the St.

landmarks.name: Postcards
landmarks.fact: Staten Island's 9/11 memorial, shaped like two folded postcards.
landmarks.about: Postcards is an outdoor sculpture in St. George, Staten Island, New York City, United States.
landmarks.credit: Jackie from Monmouth County, NJ, USA CC BY 2.0

landmarks.name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
landmarks.fact: Built in 1833 as a home for retired sailors.
landmarks.about: Snug Harbor is an 83-acre (34 ha) campus containing more than two dozen architecturally significant buildings set along the Kill Van Kull on the North Shore of Staten Island in New York City, New York, US.

landmarks.name: Wagner College
landmarks.fact: Its hilltop campus looks out over New York Harbor.
landmarks.about: Wagner College is a private college in Staten Island, New York, United States. It was established in 1883 and, as of the 2023–2024 academic year, it enrolled approximately 1,932 students, including 1,592 undergraduates and 340 graduates.

landmarks.name: Silver Lake Park
landmarks.fact: Its lake is really a reservoir for the island's water.

landmarks.name: Tompkinsville Park
landmarks.fact: Near the spot where Henry Hudson's crew got fresh water in 1609.
landmarks.about: Tompkinsville is a neighborhood in northeastern Staten Island in New York City. Named for Daniel D.
