landmarks.name: Fort Wadsworth
landmarks.fact: One of the oldest military sites in the country, guarding the Narrows.
landmarks.about: Fort Wadsworth is a former United States military installation on Staten Island in New York City, situated on The Narrows, which divide New York Bay into Upper and Lower bays, a natural point for defense of the Upper Bay, Manhattan, and beyond.

targets.name: Katz's Delicatessen
targets.fact: Serving pastrami since 1888.
targets.about: Katz's Delicatessen, also known as Katz's of New York City, is a Jewish deli at 205 East Houston Street, on the southwest corner of Houston and Ludlow Streets on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the legendary Jewish deli located on the corner of Houston and Ludlow Streets serving cured meat since 1888.

targets.name: Joe's Pizza
targets.fact: The classic Carmine Street slice since 1975.
targets.about: Joe's Pizza, also called Famous Joe's Pizza, is a pizzeria located in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, New York City on Carmine Street near Bleecker Street. The restaurant is known for serving a classic New York street-style pizza and has been called a "Greenwich Village institution".
targets.riddle: Find this Greenwich Village institution for a classic street-style slice on Carmine Street near Bleecker Street.

targets.name: Russ & Daughters
targets.fact: An 'appetizing' shop open since 1914.
targets.about: Russ & Daughters is an appetizing store that opened in 1914. It is located at 179 East Houston Street, on the Lower East Side of Manhattan, New York City.
targets.riddle: Visit this appetizing shop on the Lower East Side located at 179 East Houston Street to taste history since 1914.

targets.name: Levain Bakery
targets.fact: Famous for six-ounce cookies.
targets.about: Levain Bakery, pronounced as (luh-ven), is a retail bakery that opened in 1995 and is located at 167 West 74th Street, on the Upper West Side neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City.
targets.riddle: Visit the Upper West Side to find the home of famous six-ounce treats that have delighted since the mid-nineties.

targets.name: Magnolia Bakery
targets.fact: Its cupcakes starred on Sex and the City.
targets.about: Magnolia Bakery is a chain of bakeries founded in New York City. The first location opened in 1996 at 401 Bleecker Street, on the corner of West 11th Street in the West Village neighborhood of Manhattan.
targets.riddle: Visit the West Village corner where sweet treats gained fame on a hit show about city life.

targets.name: Sylvia's
targets.fact: The Queen of Soul Food, open since 1962.
targets.about: Sylvia's Restaurant of Harlem, often called Sylvia's Soul Food or just Sylvia's, is a soul food restaurant located at 328 Malcolm X Boulevard, between 126th and 127th Streets, in Harlem, Manhattan, New York City.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Visit the Queen of this savory cuisine located on Malcolm X Boulevard between 126th and 127th Streets in Harlem.

targets.name: Tavern on the Green
targets.fact: Built in 1870 as a sheepfold for Central Park's sheep.
targets.about: Tavern on the Green is an American cuisine restaurant in Central Park in Manhattan, New York City, near the intersection of Central Park West and West 66th Street on the Upper West Side. The restaurant, housed in a former sheepfold, has been operated by Jim Caiola and David Salama since 2014.
targets.riddle: Once a home for woolly grazers, this American eatery now welcomes diners within the heart of the park.

targets.name: Nom Wah Tea Parlor
targets.fact: Chinatown's oldest dim sum parlor, opened 1920.
targets.about: Nom Wah Tea Parlor (Chinese: 南華茶室; Cantonese Yale: Nàahm Wàh Chàhsāt; lit. 'South China Tea House'), opened in 1920, is the oldest continuously running restaurant in the Chinatown of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Visit the oldest continuously running dim sum spot in Manhattan's Chinatown to enjoy a historic taste of South China.

targets.name: Ferrara Bakery
targets.fact: Little Italy pastry shop since 1892.
targets.about: Ferrara Bakery and Cafe, established in 1892 by Antonio Ferrara, claims to be America's first espresso bar. It is located in Little Italy, Manhattan, New York City, and offers Italian delicacies.
targets.riddle: In Little Italy, find the historic spot that serves as the nation's earliest destination for a perfect cup of espresso.

targets.name: Veselka
targets.fact: Ukrainian pierogi around the clock since 1954.
targets.about: Veselka is a Ukrainian restaurant at 144 Second Avenue in the East Village neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It was established in 1954 by Wolodymyr Darmochwal (Ukrainian: Володимир Дармохвал) and his wife, Olha Darmochwal (Ukrainian: Ольга Дармохвал), post–World War II Ukrainian refugees.
targets.riddle: Visit this East Village spot for traditional dumplings served at any hour, a legacy started by refugees after the global conflict.

targets.name: Lombardi's
targets.fact: Often called America's first pizzeria.
targets.about: Lombardi's is a pizzeria at 32 Spring Street on the corner of Mott Street in the Nolita neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the nation's original pie shop located where Spring meets Mott in the heart of Nolita.

targets.name: Gray's Papaya
targets.fact: Hot dogs and papaya drinks on the Upper West Side.
targets.riddle: Visit this Upper West Side spot for a classic tubular snack paired with a refreshing tropical fruit beverage.

targets.name: Junior's
targets.fact: Cheesecake in the heart of the Theater District.
targets.about: Junior's is a restaurant chain with the original location at 386 Flatbush Avenue Extension at the corner of DeKalb Avenue in Downtown Brooklyn, New York City. Other locations include the Times Square area and the lobby of the Fox Tower in the Foxwoods Resort in  Ledyard, Connecticut.
targets.riddle: Find a slice of famous dessert within the heart of the bustling Theater District.
targets.credit: Eden, Janine and Jim from New York City CC BY 2.0

targets.name: Shake Shack Madison Square Park
targets.fact: The original Shake Shack started as a hot dog cart.
targets.about: Shake Shack is an American multinational fast casual restaurant chain based in New York City. It started out as a hot dog cart inside Madison Square Park in 2001, and its popularity steadily grew.
targets.riddle: Find the park where a humble hot dog cart blossomed into a famous global eatery.

targets.name: Keens Steakhouse
targets.fact: Its ceiling holds thousands of clay pipes.
targets.about: Keens Steakhouse (formerly Keen's English Chop House) is a steakhouse restaurant located at 72 West 36th Street (between Fifth Avenue and Sixth Avenue) in the Garment District in Manhattan, New York City.
targets.riddle: Look up to find thousands of clay pipes hanging above where you enjoy a classic chop in the Garment District.

targets.name: Balthazar
targets.fact: A Paris-style brasserie in SoHo.
targets.about: Balthazar is a French brasserie restaurant located at 80 Spring Street (between Broadway and Crosby Street) in SoHo in Manhattan, in New York City. It opened on April 21, 1997, and is owned by British-born restaurateur Keith McNally.
targets.riddle: Find this Paris-style brasserie in SoHo, located between Broadway and Crosby Street, opened by a British-born restaurateur.

targets.name: Minetta Tavern
targets.fact: A Greenwich Village tavern dating to 1937.
targets.about: Minetta Tavern is a restaurant owned by Keith McNally in Greenwich Village. In 2009, Frank Bruni of The New York Times gave the Tavern three stars.
targets.riddle: Find this historic Greenwich Village spot where a critic awarded stars to a dining establishment owned by Keith McNally.

targets.name: Delmonico's
targets.fact: Where the Delmonico steak got its name.
targets.about: Delmonico's is a series of restaurants that have operated in New York City, with the present version located at 56 Beaver Street in the Financial District of Manhattan. The original version opened in 1827 at 23 William Street.
targets.riddle: Visit the Financial District home where a famous signature steak first earned its legendary name.

targets.name: Fraunces Tavern
targets.fact: Washington bid farewell to his officers here in 1783.
targets.about: Fraunces Tavern is a museum, bar and restaurant in New York City, situated at 54 Pearl Street at the corner of Pearl and Broad Streets in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan. Fraunces Tavern played a prominent role in history before, during, and after the American Revolution.
targets.riddle: Visit the Financial District corner where the general once bid farewell to his officers before the revolution concluded.

targets.name: Chelsea Market
targets.fact: The old Nabisco factory where the Oreo was invented.
targets.about: Chelsea Market is a food hall, shopping mall, office building and television production facility located in the Chelsea neighborhood of the borough of Manhattan, in New York City.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Visit the former factory where the famous dark sandwich cookie was invented to explore this bustling food hall.

targets.name: Zabar's
targets.fact: An Upper West Side food emporium since 1934.
targets.about: Zabar's ( ZAY-barz) is an appetizing store at 2245 Broadway and 80th Street, on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, founded by Louis and Lillian Zabar. It is known for its selection of bagels, smoked fish, olives, and cheeses.
targets.riddle: Find this Upper West Side appetizing institution where Broadway meets the street known for bagels, smoked fish, and fine cheeses.

targets.name: Barney Greengrass
targets.fact: 'The Sturgeon King' since 1908.
targets.about: Barney Greengrass is a restaurant, deli, and appetizing store at 541 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 86th and 87th Streets) on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, New York City, started in 1908.
targets.riddle: Visit this Upper West Side appetizing store on Amsterdam Avenue known as The Sturgeon King since its inception.

targets.name: Serendipity 3
targets.fact: Home of the Frrrozen Hot Chocolate.
targets.about: Serendipity 3, often written Serendipity III, is a restaurant located at 225 East 60th Street, between Second and Third avenues in New York City, founded by Calvin L Holt, Patch Caradine and Stephen Bruce in 1954.
targets.riddle: Visit the East side home of a famous chilly cocoa treat founded by a trio near Second and Third avenues.

targets.name: Rao's
targets.fact: Ten tables, nearly impossible to book.
targets.about: Rao's () is an Italian-American restaurant founded in 1896. It is located at 455 East 114th Street, on the corner of Pleasant Avenue in East Harlem (or Italian Harlem), New York City.
targets.riddle: Secure one of the ten tables at this legendary Italian-American corner spot on Pleasant Avenue in East Harlem.

targets.name: Dominique Ansel Bakery
targets.fact: Birthplace of the Cronut.
targets.about: Dominique Ansel (born 1978) is a French pastry chef and owner of Dominique Ansel Bakery in New York City. He is the inventor of the Cronut, a croissant-donut hybrid.
targets.riddle: Visit this French pastry chef's shop to find the famous hybrid treat that is both croissant and donut.

targets.name: Pete's Tavern
targets.fact: Claims to be NYC's oldest continuously operating bar.
targets.about: Pete's Tavern, located at 129 East 18th Street on the corner of Irving Place in the Gramercy Park neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, is a pub food restaurant and the oldest continuously operating restaurant and bar in New York City.
targets.credit: Dmadeo; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 02:20, 28 April 2011 (UTC) CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: Find the historic spot on Irving Place and East eighteenth Street that serves pub food and never stops operating.

targets.name: P.J. Clarke's
targets.fact: A saloon from 1884 that refused to be torn down.
targets.about: P. J.
targets.riddle: Seek a historic saloon that stood its ground and refused to be torn down.

targets.name: Mamoun's Falafel
targets.fact: Serving falafel on MacDougal since 1971.
targets.riddle: Find this legendary Middle Eastern treat on MacDougal, where hungry crowds have gathered for decades.

targets.name: Red Rooster
targets.fact: Marcus Samuelsson's Harlem restaurant.
targets.riddle: Visit the famous Harlem establishment founded by Marcus Samuelsson for a soulful dining experience.

targets.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
targets.fact: More than two million works across 5,000 years.
targets.about: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, colloquially referred to as the Met, is an encyclopedic art museum in New York City. By floor area, it is the third-largest museum in the world and the largest art museum in the Americas.
targets.riddle: Explore the largest house of creativity in the Americas, boasting a vast collection spanning thousands of cycles.

targets.name: Museum of Modern Art
targets.fact: Home of Van Gogh's The Starry Night.
targets.about: The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) is an art museum located in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, on 53rd Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues.
targets.riddle: Visit this Midtown home on the street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues to see Van Gogh's swirling night sky.

targets.name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
targets.fact: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral opened in 1959.
targets.about: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, often referred to as The Guggenheim, is an art museum at 1071 Fifth Avenue between 88th and 89th Streets on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Ascend the spiraling path of this famous art destination located between eighty-eighth and eighty-ninth streets on Fifth Avenue.

targets.name: American Museum of Natural History
targets.fact: Its blue whale model is 94 feet long.
targets.about: The American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) is a natural history museum on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Visit the Upper West Side to gaze upon a massive blue creature suspended within this iconic Manhattan cultural landmark.

targets.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
targets.fact: Founded by sculptor Gertrude Vanderbilt Whitney.
targets.about: The Whitney Museum of American Art (known informally as "The Whitney") is a modern and contemporary American art museum in the Meatpacking District and West Village neighborhoods of Manhattan in New York City, New York, United States.
targets.riddle: Seek the sculptor's namesake gallery of modern works tucked between the Meatpacking District and the West Village.

targets.name: Intrepid Museum
targets.fact: An aircraft carrier turned museum.
targets.about: The Intrepid Museum (originally the Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum) is a military, aerospace, and history museum in New York City, United States. It is located at Pier 86 at 46th Street, along the Hudson River, in the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood on the West Side of Manhattan.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Docked at Pier eighty-six, this historic vessel now hosts an aerospace collection along the banks of the Hudson River.

targets.name: New York Public Library
targets.fact: Guarded by the lions Patience and Fortitude.
targets.about: The Stephen A. Schwarzman Building (commonly known as the Main Branch, the 42nd Street Library, or just the New York Public Library) is the flagship building in the New York Public Library system in the Midtown neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Seek the Midtown home where two stone beasts named Patience and Fortitude guard a vast world of written treasures.

targets.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
targets.fact: Two pools sit in the footprints of the Twin Towers.
targets.about: The National September 11 Memorial & Museum (also known as the 9/11 Memorial & Museum) is a memorial and museum that are part of the World Trade Center complex, in New York City, created for remembering the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks which killed 2,977 people, as well as the February 26, 1993, World Trade Center bombing which killed six.
targets.riddle: Reflect by twin sunken basins where the trade complex once stood to honor those lost in past tragedies.

targets.name: Tenement Museum
targets.fact: Tells immigrant stories from 97 Orchard Street.
targets.about: The Lower East Side Tenement Museum is a museum and National Historic Site located at 97 and 103 Orchard Street on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in New York City, United States.
targets.riddle: Visit these Orchard Street homes on the Lower East Side to discover the preserved stories of those who arrived from abroad.

targets.name: The Met Cloisters
targets.fact: Built from pieces of medieval European abbeys.
targets.about: The Cloisters (also known as the Met Cloisters) is a museum in Fort Tryon Park, straddling the neighborhoods of Washington Heights and Inwood, in Upper Manhattan, New York City. The museum specializes in European medieval art and architecture, with a focus on the Romanesque and Gothic periods.
targets.riddle: Perched in Fort Tryon Park, this sanctuary of Romanesque and Gothic treasures was crafted from salvaged pieces of ancient European abbeys.

targets.name: The Frick Collection
targets.fact: Old Masters in Henry Clay Frick's mansion.
targets.about: The Frick Collection (colloquially known as the Frick) is an art museum on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City. It was established in 1935 to preserve the collection of the industrialist Henry Clay Frick.
targets.riddle: Visit this Upper East Side mansion to view Old Masters once owned by a famous industrialist.

targets.name: Neue Galerie
targets.fact: Home of Klimt's 'Woman in Gold'.
targets.about: The Neue Galerie New York (German for "New Gallery") is a museum of early twentieth-century German and Austrian art and design on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City. It is located in the William Starr Miller House at 86th Street and Fifth Avenue.
targets.credit: Neue Galerie New York Public domain
targets.riddle: Visit this Upper East Side mansion to gaze upon the famous portrait of a woman in gold.

targets.name: Cooper Hewitt
targets.fact: The national design museum, in Carnegie's mansion.
targets.about: Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum is a design museum at the Andrew Carnegie Mansion in Manhattan, New York City, along the Upper East Side's Museum Mile.
targets.riddle: Explore this national home for style and craft, located within a famous industrialist's historic residence on the Upper East Side.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0

targets.name: Museum of the City of New York
targets.fact: Tells the story of the city from 1609 on.
targets.about: The Museum of the City of New York (MCNY) is a history and art museum in Manhattan, New York City. It was founded by Henry Collins Brown in 1923 to preserve and present the history of New York City and its people.
targets.riddle: Visit this institution founded by Henry Collins Brown to explore the history and art of our local people.

targets.name: Studio Museum in Harlem
targets.fact: Champions artists of African descent.
targets.about: The Studio Museum in Harlem is an African-American art museum at 144 West 125th Street in the Harlem neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States.
targets.riddle: Find this cultural hub on the famous street where creators of African descent are celebrated in the heart of uptown.

targets.name: New Museum
targets.fact: Its building looks like a stack of offset boxes.
targets.about: The New Museum of Contemporary Art is a museum at 235 Bowery, on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in New York City. It was founded in 1977 by Marcia Tucker.
targets.riddle: Find the stack of offset boxes on the Bowery that has showcased contemporary art since it was founded.
targets.credit: Moritz Schmaltz from St.Gallen, Switzerland CC BY-SA 2.0

targets.name: The Morgan Library & Museum
targets.fact: J.P. Morgan's private library, with three Gutenberg Bibles.
targets.about: The Morgan Library & Museum (formerly the Pierpont Morgan Library; colloquially the Morgan) is a museum and research library in New York City, New York, United States. Completed in 1906 as the private library of the banker J.
targets.credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net). CC BY-SA 4.0
targets.riddle: Visit this former banker's private collection to view a trio of rare Gutenberg Bibles housed within his elegant study.

targets.name: New-York Historical Society
targets.fact: New York's oldest museum, founded 1804.
targets.about: The New York Historical (known as the New-York Historical Society until 2024) is an American history museum and library on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. The society was founded in 1804 as New York's first museum.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Visit the city's first institution of its kind to explore American heritage on the Upper West Side.

targets.name: Hispanic Society Museum
targets.fact: Holds works by Goya, Velazquez, and Sorolla.
targets.about: The Hispanic Society of America, now renamed the Hispanic Society Museum and Library (HSM&L), operates a museum and reference library for the study of the arts and cultures of Spain and Portugal and their former colonies in Latin America, the Spanish East Indies, and Portuguese India.
targets.riddle: Seek out masterpieces by Goya and Velazquez at this sanctuary for the arts and cultures of Spain and Portugal.

targets.name: Museum of Jewish Heritage
targets.fact: A living memorial to the Holocaust.
targets.about: The Museum of Jewish Heritage, located on Edmond J. Safra Plaza in the Battery Park City neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, is a historical museum and a memorial to those murdered in The Holocaust.
targets.riddle: Find this living memorial to those murdered in the Holocaust standing on Edmond J. Safra Plaza in Battery Park City.

targets.name: Merchant's House Museum
targets.fact: A family home frozen in the 1800s, said to be haunted.
targets.about: The Merchant's House Museum, also known as the Old Merchant's House and the Seabury Tredwell House, is a historic house museum at 29 East Fourth Street in the NoHo neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Step inside this haunted NoHo family home, where time stands still just like the spirits of the past.

targets.name: The Jewish Museum
targets.fact: Housed in the Warburg mansion on Fifth Avenue.
targets.about: The Jewish Museum is an art museum housed at 1109 Fifth Avenue, in the Felix M. Warburg House, along the Museum Mile on the Upper East Side of Manhattan, New York City.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Seek out the grand Warburg mansion along the prestigious Museum Mile where art resides within a historic Fifth Avenue home.

targets.name: Strand Bookstore
targets.fact: Famous for its '18 miles of books'.
targets.about: The Strand Bookstore is an independent bookstore located at 828 Broadway, at the corner of East 12th Street in the East Village neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, two blocks south of Union Square.
targets.riddle: Visit this East Village corner to wander through eighteen miles of shelves filled with countless stories and literary treasures.

targets.name: Jefferson Market Library
targets.fact: A former courthouse turned library.
targets.about: The Jefferson Market Branch of the New York Public Library, once known as the Jefferson Market Courthouse, is a National Historic Landmark located at 425 Avenue of the Americas (Sixth Avenue), on the southwest corner of West 10th Street, in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, New York City, on a triangular plot formed by Greenwich Avenue and West 10th Street.
targets.riddle: Once a place of legal judgment, this triangular Greenwich Village landmark now serves as a quiet home for books.

targets.name: Central Park Zoo
targets.fact: Its sea lion feedings draw crowds daily.
targets.about: The Central Park Zoo is a 6.5-acre (2.6 ha) zoo located at the southeast corner of Central Park in New York City. It is part of an integrated system of four zoos and one aquarium managed by the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS).
targets.riddle: Watch the aquatic mammals enjoy their daily meals at this southeast corner attraction managed by the wildlife society.

targets.name: The High Line
targets.fact: A park built on an old freight rail line.
targets.about: The High Line is a 1.45-mile-long (2.33 km) elevated linear park, greenway, and rail trail created on a former New York Central Railroad spur on the West Side of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Stroll along this elevated greenway built upon a former freight rail spur located on the busy West Side.

targets.name: Little Island
targets.fact: A park floating on 132 tulip-shaped concrete pots.
targets.about: Little Island at Pier 55 (stylized as Little Island @Pier55) is an artificial island and a public park within Hudson River Park, just off the western coast of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Stroll across a floating garden supported by tulip-shaped concrete pots resting above the western Hudson River waves.

targets.name: Bryant Park
targets.fact: Winter brings a free ice rink.
targets.about: Bryant Park is a 9.6-acre (3.9 ha), privately managed public park in the New York City borough of Manhattan. It is located between Fifth Avenue and Avenue of the Americas (Sixth Avenue) and between 40th and 42nd Streets in Midtown Manhattan.
targets.riddle: Find this midtown oasis between the fifth and sixth avenues, where a seasonal frozen path awaits your skates.

targets.name: The Battery
targets.fact: The southern tip of Manhattan.
targets.about: The Battery, formerly known as Battery Park, is a 25-acre (10 ha) public park located at the southern tip of Manhattan Island in New York City facing New York Harbor.
targets.riddle: Find this coastal public space located at the very bottom of the island where the harbor meets the city.

targets.name: Madison Square Park
targets.fact: Once home to the Statue of Liberty's torch.
targets.about: Madison Square is a public square formed by the intersection of Fifth Avenue and Broadway at 23rd Street in the New York City borough of Manhattan. The square was named for Founding Father James Madison, the fourth president of the United States.
targets.riddle: Visit the intersection where the fourth president's namesake square once held the torch of the lady in the harbor.

targets.name: Tompkins Square Park
targets.fact: Birthplace of the Hare Krishna movement in the US.
targets.about: Tompkins Square Park is a 10.5-acre (4.2 ha) public park in the Alphabet City portion of East Village, Manhattan, New York City. The square-shaped park, bounded on the north by East 10th Street, on the east by Avenue B, on the south by East 7th Street, and on the west by Avenue A, is abutted by St.
targets.riddle: Find the historic roots of the Hare Krishna movement within this square space nestled between Avenue A and Avenue B.

targets.name: Fort Tryon Park
targets.fact: Designed by the Olmsted Brothers, given by Rockefeller.
targets.about: Fort Tryon Park is a public park located in the Washington Heights and Inwood neighborhoods of the borough of Manhattan in New York City. The 67-acre (27 ha) park is situated on a ridge in Upper Manhattan, close to the Hudson River to the west.
targets.riddle: Gifted by a billionaire, this ridge-top sanctuary overlooks the river in the northern reaches of the island.

targets.name: Inwood Hill Park
targets.fact: Home to Manhattan's last natural forest.
targets.about: Inwood Hill Park is a 196 acres (79 ha) public park in the Inwood neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, operated by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation.
targets.riddle: Seek the northern tip of the island to discover the final patch of wilderness left in its original state.

targets.name: Marcus Garvey Park
targets.fact: Its fire watchtower dates to 1857.
targets.about: Marcus Garvey Park (formerly and also named Mount Morris Park) is a 20.16-acre (81,600 m2) park on the border between the Harlem and East Harlem neighborhoods of Manhattan, New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the historic iron lookout standing between Harlem and its eastern neighbor within this twenty-acre green escape.

targets.name: Morningside Park
targets.fact: A cliffside park designed by Olmsted and Vaux.
targets.about: Morningside Park is a 30-acre (12-hectare) public park in Upper Manhattan in New York City, New York, United States. The park is bounded by 110th Street to the south, 123rd Street to the north, Morningside Avenue to the east, and Morningside Drive to the west.
targets.riddle: Designed by the creators of Central, this cliffside escape sits between the avenue and the drive in Upper Manhattan.

targets.name: Sheep Meadow
targets.fact: Sheep grazed here until 1934.
targets.about: Sheep Meadow is a 15-acre (61,000 m2) meadow near the southwestern section of Central Park, between West 66th and 69th Streets in Manhattan, New York City.
targets.riddle: Woolly creatures once wandered this fifteen-acre lawn nestled in the southwestern corner of the city's grandest urban green space.

targets.name: Conservatory Garden
targets.fact: Central Park's only formal garden.
targets.about: The Conservatory Garden is a formal garden near the northeastern corner of Central Park in Upper Manhattan, New York City. Comprising 6 acres (24,000 m2), it is the only formal garden in Central Park.
targets.riddle: Seek the solitary structured oasis nestled within the northeastern corner of our city's most famous green space.

targets.name: Seward Park
targets.fact: Home to one of the first municipal playgrounds in the US.
targets.about: Seward Park is a public park and playground on the Lower East Side of Manhattan, New York City. Located north of East Broadway and east of Essex Street, it is 3.046 acres (12,330 m2) in size and is the first municipally built playground in the United States.
targets.credit: This photo was taken by participant/team Sheila as part of the Commons:Wikipedia CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: Visit this Lower East Side site, home to the very first playground built by the city in the country.

targets.name: Columbus Park
targets.fact: Chinatown's park, once the notorious Five Points.
targets.about: Columbus Park formerly known as Mulberry Bend Park, Five Points Park and Paradise Park, is a public park in Chinatown, Manhattan, in New York City that was built in 1897.
targets.riddle: Once the notorious Five Points, this Chinatown space was formerly known by names like Mulberry Bend and Paradise.

targets.name: Stuyvesant Square
targets.fact: Land donated by Peter Stuyvesant's descendant.
targets.about: Stuyvesant Square is the name of both a park and its surrounding neighborhood in the New York City borough of Manhattan. The park is located between 15th Street, 17th Street, Rutherford Place, and Nathan D.
targets.riddle: Once gifted by a descendant of a famous governor, this green space sits just off Rutherford Place.

targets.name: St. Nicholas Park
targets.fact: A steep park below City College.
targets.about: St. Nicholas Park is a public park in Manhattan, New York City, between the neighborhoods of Harlem, Hamilton Heights and Manhattanville.
targets.riddle: Find this steep green space tucked away beneath the local college, resting between Harlem, Hamilton Heights, and Manhattanville.

targets.name: Highbridge Water Tower
targets.fact: Once held water from the Croton Aqueduct.
targets.riddle: Ascend to the stone structure that once held precious liquid flowing from the famous aqueduct.

targets.name: Paley Park
targets.fact: A tiny pocket park with a 20-foot waterfall.
targets.about: Paley Park is a pocket park located at 3 East 53rd Street between Madison and Fifth Avenues in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, on the former site of the Stork Club. Designed by the landscape architectural firm of Zion Breen Richardson Associates, it opened May 23, 1967.
targets.riddle: Find this tiny midtown oasis between Madison and Fifth, where a cascading wall of water replaced a former famous club.

targets.name: Rockefeller Park
targets.fact: Battery Park City's riverside lawn.
targets.about: Rockefeller Park is a city park named in honor of oil magnate John D. Rockefeller Sr., located in Cleveland, Ohio.
targets.riddle: Find the riverside lawn nestled within Battery Park City that honors a famous oil magnate.

targets.name: The Great Lawn
targets.fact: Built over the filled-in old reservoir.
targets.about: The Great Lawn and Turtle Pond are two connected features of Central Park in Manhattan, New York City, United States. The lawn and pond are located on the site of a former reservoir for the Croton Aqueduct system which was infilled during the early 20th century.
targets.riddle: Once a basin for the Croton Aqueduct system, this green space now sits where the old reservoir was filled in.

targets.name: Sara D. Roosevelt Park
targets.fact: A long, narrow park on the Lower East Side.
targets.about: Sara Delano Roosevelt Park is a 7.8-acre (3.2 ha) park on the Lower East Side of the New York City borough of Manhattan.
targets.credit: This photo was taken by participant/team Team Dustizeff as part of the Commons:W CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: Stretching thin across the Lower East Side, this narrow strip of greenery offers an escape within the borough of Manhattan.

targets.name: Alice in Wonderland Statue
targets.fact: Kids are encouraged to climb it.
targets.about: The Alice in Wonderland is a sculpture located at Central Park in Manhattan, New York City, U.S. It is approximately at 74th Street, on the north side of Conservatory Water.
targets.credit: atp tyreseus / Jere Keys from San Francisco, USA Public domain
targets.riddle: Climb upon this bronze sculpture found near the north side of Conservatory Water within the city's famous central garden.

targets.name: Fearless Girl
targets.fact: She now stares down the New York Stock Exchange.
targets.about: Fearless Girl is a bronze sculpture by Kristen Visbal of a 4-foot-high (1.2 m) girl standing in a self-confident pose. It is located in New York City on Broad Street across from the New York Stock Exchange Building in the Financial District of Manhattan.
targets.riddle: Standing on Broad Street with self-confident pose, I stare down the building where stocks are traded in the financial district.
targets.credit: Billie Grace Ward from New York, USA CC BY 2.0

targets.name: Cleopatra's Needle
targets.fact: An Egyptian obelisk about 3,500 years old.
targets.about: Cleopatra's Needle in New York City is one of a pair of obelisks, together named Cleopatra's Needles, that were moved from the ruins of the Caesareum of Alexandria, Ancient Egypt, in the 19th century.
targets.riddle: I am a pair of ancient stone pillars moved from the ruins of the Caesareum to rest in the city.

targets.name: St. Paul's Chapel
targets.fact: Manhattan's oldest surviving church, from 1766.
targets.about: St. Paul's Chapel is a chapel building of Trinity Church, an Episcopal parish, at 209 Broadway, between Fulton Street and Vesey Street, in Lower Manhattan, New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the oldest surviving house of worship on Broadway, nestled between Fulton and Vesey in Lower Manhattan.

targets.name: Woolworth Building
targets.fact: Nicknamed the 'Cathedral of Commerce'.
targets.about: The Woolworth Building is a 792-foot-tall (241 m) residential building and early skyscraper at 233 Broadway in the Tribeca neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City, United States. Designed by Cass Gilbert in the Neo-Gothic style, the Woolworth Building was originally an office skyscraper.
targets.riddle: Find this Neo-Gothic Cathedral of Commerce standing tall on Broadway as a former office skyscraper in the Tribeca neighborhood.

targets.name: African Burial Ground
targets.fact: Resting place of about 15,000 free and enslaved Africans.
targets.about: African Burial Ground National Monument is a monument at Duane Street and African Burial Ground Way (Elk Street) in the Civic Center section of Lower Manhattan, New York City. Its main building is the Ted Weiss Federal Building at 290 Broadway.
targets.riddle: In the Civic Center, visit the resting place of thousands near Duane Street and the Federal Building.

targets.name: Irish Hunger Memorial
targets.fact: A real Irish cottage on a slice of Irish landscape.
targets.about: The Irish Hunger Memorial (Irish: Cuimhneachán Ghorta Mhóir na hÉireann) is a 0.5-acre (0.20 ha) park at the corner of Vesey Street and North End Avenue in the Battery Park City neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.
targets.credit: David Shankbone at en.wikipedia CC BY 2.5
targets.riddle: Seek a transplanted rural dwelling resting upon a grassy patch where Vesey Street meets North End Avenue.

targets.name: Duke Ellington Memorial
targets.fact: Duke stands beside his piano on columns held by nine muses.
targets.about: The Duke Ellington Memorial by Robert Graham is installed at Duke Ellington Circle in Manhattan, New York City, New York. The monument depicts Duke Ellington at a piano, supported by three columns depicting three caryatids each, known as his nine muses.
targets.riddle: Seek the legend standing at his keys, held aloft by nine muses upon a circle in the city.

targets.name: LOVE Sculpture
targets.fact: Robert Indiana's famous tilted O.
targets.riddle: Seek out the famous tilted letter that leans in this city.

targets.name: Tiffany & Co. Fifth Avenue
targets.fact: Where Holly Golightly had breakfast.
targets.about: The Tiffany and Company Building, also known as the Tiffany Building and 401 Fifth Avenue, is an eight-story commercial building at Fifth Avenue and 37th Street in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City, New York, United States.
targets.riddle: Visit the Midtown location where a famous lady once enjoyed her morning meal.

targets.name: The Ansonia
targets.fact: Once kept a small farm on its roof.
targets.about: The Ansonia (formerly the Ansonia Hotel) is a condominium building at 2109 Broadway, between 73rd and 74th Streets, on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, United States. The 17-story structure was designed by French architect Paul Emile Duboy in the Beaux-Arts style.
targets.riddle: Seek the Beaux-Arts structure on Broadway where a tiny farm once flourished atop its seventeen stories.

targets.name: Cooper Union Foundation Building
targets.fact: Lincoln gave a career-making speech here in 1860.
targets.about: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art, commonly known as Cooper Union, is a private college on Cooper Square in Manhattan, New York City. Peter Cooper founded the institution in 1859 after learning about the government-supported École Polytechnique in France.
targets.riddle: Visit the square where a famous leader delivered a career-making speech at the institution Peter established for science and art.

targets.name: Temple Emanu-El
targets.fact: One of the largest synagogues in the world.
targets.about: Congregation Emanu-El of New York is the oldest Reform Jewish congregation in New York City. It has served as a flagship congregation in the Reform branch of Judaism since its founding in 1845.
targets.riddle: Visit one of the largest houses of worship where the oldest Reform branch of the faith gathers in this city.

targets.name: Federal Hall
targets.fact: Where Washington took the oath as first President.
targets.about: Federal Hall was the first capitol building of the United States established under the Constitution.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Visit the site where the inaugural leader swore his oath to serve as the nation's primary capitol under the Constitution.

targets.name: Castle Clinton
targets.fact: A fort that became America's first immigration station.
targets.about: Castle Clinton (also known as Fort Clinton and Castle Garden) is a restored circular sandstone fort within Battery Park at the southern end of Manhattan in New York City, United States. Built from 1808 to 1811, it was the first American immigration station, predating Ellis Island.
targets.riddle: Find this circular sandstone fort in Battery Park that served as the nation's first station for those arriving from abroad.

targets.name: Sherman Monument
targets.fact: A gilded general led by the figure of Victory.
targets.riddle: A gilded general is led forward by the figure of Victory near the park.

targets.name: Trinity Church
targets.fact: Alexander Hamilton is buried in its churchyard.
targets.about: Trinity Church is a historic parish in the Episcopal Diocese of New York. The church is located at 89 Broadway opposite Wall Street, in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan in New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the historic Financial District parish where the famous Alexander Hamilton rests within the quiet churchyard.

targets.name: Bow Bridge
targets.fact: Central Park's most-filmed bridge.
targets.riddle: Cross the most-filmed path within this park to find a classic span captured on screen more than any other.

targets.name: Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument
targets.fact: A marble temple honoring Union soldiers.
targets.about: The Soldiers' and Sailors' Memorial Monument is located in Riverside Park, at the intersection of 89th Street and Riverside Drive, on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. It commemorates Union Army soldiers and sailors who served in the American Civil War.
targets.riddle: Perched in a park, this marble temple honors those who served at sea and on land during the conflict.

targets.name: Eldridge Street Synagogue
targets.fact: One of the first great synagogues built by Eastern European Jews in the US.
targets.about: The Eldridge Street Synagogue is an Orthodox Jewish synagogue at 12–16 Eldridge Street in the Chinatown and Lower East Side neighborhoods of Manhattan in New York City. Built in 1887 for Congregation Kahal Adath Jeshurun, the synagogue is one of the first erected in the U.S. by Eastern European Jews.
targets.riddle: Seek this early house of worship built by Eastern European Jews nestled between Chinatown and the Lower East Side.

targets.name: Juliana's Pizza
targets.fact: Coal-oven pizza from Patsy Grimaldi, a legend of NYC pizza.
targets.about: Juliana's is a pizzeria located in Brooklyn, New York, founded in 2012 by Pasquale "Patsy" Grimaldi and named after his mother. In 2015, it was rated the best pizzeria in the United States on TripAdvisor.
targets.riddle: Visit this Brooklyn spot, founded by a legend and named for his mother, to taste the best slice in the country.

targets.name: Peter Luger Steak House
targets.fact: Serving porterhouse steaks since 1887, and cash-only for decades.
targets.about: Peter Luger Steak House is a steakhouse located in the Williamsburg section of Brooklyn, New York City, with a second location in Great Neck, New York, in the western part of Long Island.
targets.riddle: Bring your paper bills to this Williamsburg institution for a legendary porterhouse that has been served for over a century.

targets.name: Junior's Restaurant
targets.fact: The original home of Junior's famous cheesecake, since 1950.
targets.about: Junior's is a restaurant chain with the original location at 386 Flatbush Avenue Extension at the corner of DeKalb Avenue in Downtown Brooklyn, New York City. Other locations include the Times Square area and the lobby of the Fox Tower in the Foxwoods Resort in  Ledyard, Connecticut.
targets.riddle: Find the corner of Flatbush Avenue Extension and DeKalb Avenue to taste a famous dessert served since 1950.

targets.name: Lucali
targets.fact: A candlelit pizza spot with no phone reservations and long lines.
targets.about: Lucali is a pizzeria founded by Mark Iacono in 2006, located in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, New York City. The pizzeria serves brick oven pizza and calzones.
targets.riddle: Wait in a long line for brick oven pies or calzones at this candlelit Carroll Gardens spot that takes no reservations.

targets.name: Sahadi's
targets.fact: A Middle Eastern grocery on Atlantic Avenue since 1948.
targets.about: Sahadi's  is a shop in Brooklyn, New York City. The business was established in Manhattan in 1895, and relocated to Brooklyn in 1941.
targets.riddle: Find this Middle Eastern grocery on Atlantic Avenue that moved from Manhattan to Brooklyn long ago.

targets.name: Time Out Market New York
targets.fact: A food hall in a Civil War-era warehouse with a rooftop view.
targets.about: Empire Stores is a former warehouse complex along the waterfront Brooklyn Bridge Park within the neighborhood of Dumbo, Brooklyn, New York City, in the U.S. state of New York.
targets.credit: R.scholz at English Wikipedia CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: Dine in a Civil War-era waterfront warehouse within Dumbo and head to the rooftop for a view of the park.

targets.name: Brooklyn Brewery
targets.fact: Its logo was designed by Milton Glaser, who also made I ♥ NY.
targets.about: Brooklyn Brewery is a brewery in Brooklyn, New York, United States. It was started in 1988 by Steve Hindy and Tom Potter.
targets.riddle: Visit the borough home to the craft taproom whose iconic branding was created by the designer of I ♥ NY.

targets.name: Brooklyn Museum
targets.fact: One of the largest art museums in the US, with 1.5 million works.
targets.about: The Brooklyn Museum is an art museum in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. At 560,000 square feet (52,000 m2), the museum is New York City's second largest and contains an art collection with around 500,000 objects.
targets.riddle: Explore this borough’s vast home to half a million objects, ranking second in size across the entire city.

targets.name: Brooklyn Academy of Music
targets.fact: America's oldest performing arts center still running, since 1861.
targets.about: The Brooklyn Academy of Music (BAM) is a multi-arts center in Brooklyn, New York City. It hosts progressive and avant-garde performances, with theater, dance, music, opera, film programming across multiple nearby venues.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Visit this historic multi-arts center to experience progressive theater, dance, and film in the heart of the borough.

targets.name: New York Transit Museum
targets.fact: It lives inside a real 1936 subway station.
targets.about: The New York Transit Museum (also called the NYC Transit Museum) is a museum that displays historical artifacts of the New York City Subway, bus, and commuter rail systems in the greater New York City metropolitan region.
targets.riddle: Descend into a decommissioned subterranean stop to explore historical artifacts of the city's vast rail and bus networks.

targets.name: Center for Brooklyn History
targets.fact: Holds the borough's archives, from maps to Dodgers memorabilia.
targets.about: The Center for Brooklyn History (CBH, formerly known as the Brooklyn Historical Society) is a museum, library, and educational center founded in 1863 that preserves and encourages the study of Brooklyn's 400-year history.
targets.riddle: Visit this home for archives, maps, and baseball treasures that preserve the storied past of our entire borough.

targets.name: St. Ann's Warehouse
targets.fact: A theater built inside the walls of an 1860s tobacco warehouse.
targets.about: St. Ann's Warehouse is a performing arts organization in Brooklyn, New York City.
targets.riddle: Find this performing arts space hidden within the brick walls of a former tobacco storage building in Brooklyn.

targets.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
targets.fact: Its cherry blossom festival draws huge crowds every spring.
targets.about: Brooklyn Botanic Garden (BBG) is a botanical garden in the borough of Brooklyn in New York City. The botanical garden occupies 52 acres (21 ha) in central Brooklyn, close to Mount Prospect Park, Prospect Park, and the Brooklyn Museum.
targets.riddle: Visit this fifty-two acre floral sanctuary in central borough lands, located right beside the grand museum and famous park.

targets.name: Cobble Hill Park
targets.fact: A tiny neighborhood park saved from becoming a supermarket.
targets.about: Cobble Hill is a neighborhood in the northwestern portion of the New York City borough of Brooklyn.
targets.riddle: Once destined to be a grocery store, this miniature neighborhood green space remains a peaceful refuge in northwestern Brooklyn.

targets.name: Commodore Barry Park
targets.fact: Brooklyn's oldest park, named for the father of the US Navy.
targets.about: Commodore Barry Park is an urban park in the Fort Greene neighborhood of the New York City borough of Brooklyn. The park is operated by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation.
targets.credit: This photo was taken by participant/team Jim Henderson as part of the Commons:Wi Public domain
targets.riddle: Visit the oldest green space in the borough, dedicated to the man known as the father of the naval fleet.

targets.name: Cadman Plaza Park
targets.fact: Home to Brooklyn's World War II memorial.
targets.about: Cadman Plaza is a park located on the border of the Brooklyn Heights and Downtown Brooklyn neighborhoods in Brooklyn, New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the memorial honoring a global conflict where downtown meets the heights in this borough green space.

targets.name: Williamsburgh Savings Bank Tower
targets.fact: Brooklyn's tallest building for 80 years, with a giant four-sided clock.
targets.about: The Williamsburgh Savings Bank Tower, also known as One Hanson Place, is a skyscraper in the Fort Greene neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City, New York, U.S.
targets.credit: Gryffindor; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 21:26, 9 October 2012 (UTC) CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: In Fort Greene stands the tallest structure, watching over the neighborhood with its giant four-sided timepiece.

targets.name: Old Stone House
targets.fact: A rebuilt 1699 farmhouse at the center of the Battle of Brooklyn.
targets.about: The Old Stone House is a house located in the Park Slope neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. It is situated within the J.
targets.riddle: Seek this rebuilt farmhouse in Park Slope that stands at the center of a historic battle.

targets.name: Plymouth Church
targets.fact: A stop on the Underground Railroad; Lincoln worshipped here.
targets.about: Plymouth Church is a Congregational church located at 57 Orange Street, between Henry and Hicks Streets, in the Brooklyn Heights neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. The Church House is located at 75 Hicks Street.
targets.riddle: Visit this Brooklyn Heights sanctuary where a president once prayed and freedom seekers found a path to safety.

targets.name: Clock Tower Building
targets.fact: Its glass clock faces frame one of NYC's most famous views.
targets.riddle: Look through these glass faces to frame one of the most famous views in the city.

targets.name: Bohemian Hall & Beer Garden
targets.fact: NYC's oldest beer garden, open since 1910.
targets.about: The Bohemian Citizens' Benevolent Society is a private benevolent society founded in 1892 in Astoria, Queens, to support Czech and Slovak immigrants to the area, as well as people of Czech and Slovak ancestry.
targets.riddle: Visit the oldest Astoria garden created by a benevolent society to support Czech and Slovak immigrants in Queens.

targets.name: Taverna Kyclades
targets.fact: A Greek seafood favorite on Ditmars Boulevard.
targets.riddle: Find this popular spot for oceanic cuisine tucked along Ditmars Boulevard.

targets.name: Elias Corner
targets.fact: Astoria's classic Greek fish taverna with no menu.
targets.riddle: In Astoria, visit this classic Greek fish taverna where you choose your meal without ever glancing at a menu.

targets.name: Court Square Diner
targets.fact: A 24-hour silver diner under the elevated tracks.
targets.riddle: Find this polished chrome eatery resting beneath the rumbling path of the overhead trains at any hour.

targets.name: MoMA PS1
targets.fact: A contemporary art space inside a former public school.
targets.about: MoMA PS1 is a contemporary art museum at 22-01 Jackson Avenue in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens, in New York City, United States.
targets.riddle: Seek out the creative works displayed within the halls of a Long Island City building that once served as a school.

targets.name: Museum of the Moving Image
targets.fact: Home to a huge collection of movie and TV props and cameras.
targets.about: The Museum of the Moving Image (MoMI) is a time-based media museum located in a former building of the historic Astoria Studios (now Kaufman Astoria Studios), in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City.
targets.riddle: Explore a former Astoria Studios building where historic cameras and iconic cinema props are now kept for public view.

targets.name: Noguchi Museum
targets.fact: Sculptor Isamu Noguchi designed it himself around a garden.
targets.about: The Noguchi Museum (chartered as The Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum) is a museum and sculpture garden at 32-37 Vernon Boulevard in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York City.
targets.riddle: Stroll through a tranquil garden retreat designed by a master sculptor in the heart of Long Island City.

targets.name: SculptureCenter
targets.fact: A contemporary sculpture space in a former trolley repair shop.
targets.about: SculptureCenter is a not-for-profit, contemporary art museum located in Long Island City, Queens, New York City. It was founded in 1928 as "The Clay Club" by Dorothea Denslow.
targets.riddle: Once a place to fix trolleys, this Long Island City space now displays modern works founded as The Clay Club.

targets.name: Socrates Sculpture Park
targets.fact: Artists turned an illegal dump into an outdoor sculpture park.
targets.about: Socrates Sculpture Park is an outdoor museum and public park where artists can create and exhibit sculptures and multi-media installations. It is located one block from the Noguchi Museum at the intersection of Broadway and Vernon Boulevard in the neighborhood of Astoria, Queens, New York City.
targets.riddle: Once an illegal dump, this Astoria space now showcases art at the intersection of Broadway and Vernon Boulevard.

targets.name: Rainey Park
targets.fact: A small riverside park named for a local who pushed for the Queensboro Bridge.
targets.riddle: Stroll by the river where a dedicated local advocated for the nearby bridge to connect our borough.

targets.name: Hunters Point South Park
targets.fact: A waterfront park with a view of the Manhattan skyline and the UN.
targets.riddle: Stare across the water at the city horizon and the world assembly from this scenic riverside green.

targets.name: Athens Square
targets.fact: A plaza with Greek columns and statues of Socrates and Athena.
targets.riddle: Visit this plaza to admire towering stone pillars alongside statues of a famous philosopher and a goddess of wisdom.

targets.name: Pepsi-Cola Sign
targets.fact: A landmark neon sign from 1936, moved to Gantry Plaza.
targets.about: The Pepsi-Cola sign is a neon sign at Gantry Plaza State Park in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York City. The sign, visible from Manhattan and the East River, was built in 1940 and originally installed atop PepsiCo (previously Pepsi-Cola)'s bottling factory nearby.
targets.riddle: Visible from Manhattan, this glowing relic once sat atop a bottling factory and now shines at Gantry Plaza State Park.

targets.name: Hell Gate Bridge
targets.fact: It was the world's longest steel arch bridge when it opened in 1917.
targets.about: The Hell Gate Bridge (originally the New York Connecting Railroad Bridge) is a railroad bridge in New York City. The bridge carries two tracks of Amtrak's Northeast Corridor and one freight track between Astoria, Queens, and Port Morris, Bronx, via Randalls and Wards Islands.
targets.riddle: I am a massive steel arch carrying trains between Astoria and the Bronx over the islands.

targets.name: Queensboro Bridge
targets.fact: Simon & Garfunkel called it the 59th Street Bridge.
targets.about: The Queensboro, officially the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge, but known by locals by one of two other names depending on the side, is a cantilever bridge over the East River in New York City.
targets.riddle: Simon and Garfunkel sang of this cantilever path spanning the East River, which locals know by two different names.

targets.name: Arthur Avenue Retail Market
targets.fact: An indoor Italian market in the Bronx's Little Italy, since 1940.
targets.about: Arthur Avenue is a street in the Belmont neighborhood of the Bronx, New York City, which serves as the center of the Bronx's "Little Italy".
targets.riddle: Visit this indoor hub in the heart of the Belmont neighborhood to experience the authentic spirit of the local Little Italy.

targets.name: Yankee Tavern
targets.fact: A sports bar near the stadium since 1927; Babe Ruth drank here.
targets.riddle: Visit this historic sports bar near the stadium where the Great Bambino once enjoyed a drink.

targets.name: Bronx Museum of the Arts
targets.fact: A free art museum on the Grand Concourse.
targets.about: The Bronx Museum of the Arts (BxMA), also called the Bronx Museum of Art or simply the Bronx Museum, is an American cultural institution located in Concourse, Bronx, New York.
targets.riddle: Visit this free cultural institution located directly on the Grand Concourse to view impressive creative works.

targets.name: Edgar Allan Poe Cottage
targets.fact: Poe wrote Annabel Lee in this small 1812 farmhouse.
targets.about: The Edgar Allan Poe Cottage (or Poe Cottage) is the former home of American writer Edgar Allan Poe. It is located near the intersection of Kingsbridge Road and the Grand Concourse in the Fordham neighborhood of the Bronx in New York City.
targets.credit: Zoirusha at English Wikipedia Public domain
targets.riddle: Visit the Fordham farmhouse where the author of Annabel Lee once lived near the Grand Concourse.

targets.name: Bronx Zoo
targets.fact: One of the largest city zoos in the world, opened in 1899.
targets.about: The Bronx Zoo (also historically the Bronx Zoological Park and the Bronx Zoological Gardens) is a zoo within Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City.
targets.riddle: Roam within a massive city park to visit one of the largest wildlife collections on the entire planet.

targets.name: New York Botanical Garden
targets.fact: 250 acres of gardens and an old-growth forest.
targets.about: The New York Botanical Garden (NYBG) is a botanical garden at Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City. Established in 1891, it is located on a 250-acre (100 ha) site that contains a landscape with over one million living plants; the Enid A.
targets.credit: Ivo Vermeulen, Matthew Newman CC BY-SA 2.5
targets.riddle: Explore this massive Bronx landscape filled with an ancient forest and over a million living plants.

targets.name: Franz Sigel Park
targets.fact: Named for a German-born Civil War general.
targets.riddle: Honor the German-born leader of the American conflict by visiting this green space named for a Civil War general.

targets.name: Joyce Kilmer Park
targets.fact: Named for the poet who wrote 'Trees'.
targets.about: The Lorelei Fountain, also known as the Heinrich Heine Memorial, is a monument located on East 161st Street in the Concourse section of the Bronx, New York City, near the Bronx County Courthouse.
targets.riddle: Find the monument of the siren near the courthouse, dedicated to the poet who famously wrote about wooden giants.

targets.name: 1520 Sedgwick Avenue
targets.fact: The apartment building where hip hop was born in 1973.
targets.about: 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is a 102-unit apartment building in the Morris Heights neighborhood of the Bronx in New York City. Described in The New York Times as a long-time "haven for working class families", it has been historically accepted as the birthplace of hip hop.
targets.riddle: Visit the Morris Heights residence where a legendary musical movement first found its rhythm.

targets.name: Lorelei Fountain
targets.fact: A fountain honoring poet Heinrich Heine, rejected by Düsseldorf.
targets.about: The Lorelei Fountain, also known as the Heinrich Heine Memorial, is a monument located on East 161st Street in the Concourse section of the Bronx, New York City, near the Bronx County Courthouse.
targets.riddle: Rejected by a German city, this stone tribute to a poet now rests near the Bronx County Courthouse.

targets.name: Bronx General Post Office
targets.fact: Its lobby has murals painted by Ben Shahn and Bernarda Bryson.
targets.about: The Bronx General Post Office (also known as the Bronx Central Post Office or Bronx Central Annex) is a historic post office building at 558 Grand Concourse in the South Bronx in New York City, New York, U.S.
targets.riddle: Visit this Grand Concourse landmark to see vibrant lobby murals painted by Ben Shahn and Bernarda Bryson.

targets.name: Loew's Paradise Theater
targets.fact: A 1929 movie palace with a ceiling painted like a starry sky.
targets.about: The Paradise Theater (formerly the Loew's Paradise Theatre) is a theater at 2403 Grand Concourse in the Fordham neighborhood of the Bronx in New York City, New York.
targets.riddle: Look up at the ceiling to find a painted starry sky inside this historic Grand Concourse movie palace in Fordham.

targets.name: Enoteca Maria
targets.fact: Its chefs are grandmothers from around the world, cooking in rotation.
targets.riddle: Find the place where the chefs are grandmothers from around the world, cooking in rotation.

targets.name: National Lighthouse Museum
targets.fact: On the site of the old US Lighthouse Service depot.
targets.riddle: Discover the destination built on the site of the old US beacon Service depot.

targets.name: Staten Island Museum
targets.fact: Founded in 1881, it has art, science, and history under one roof.
targets.about: Staten Island Museum (officially the Staten Island Institute of Arts & Sciences) is Staten Island’s oldest cultural institution, and the only remaining general interest museum in New York City.
targets.riddle: Seek the oldest cultural institution, founded in 1881, that has art, science, and history under one roof.

targets.name: Alice Austen House
targets.fact: Home of Alice Austen, one of America's first female photographers.
targets.about: The Alice Austen House, also known as Clear Comfort,  is located at 2 Hylan Boulevard in the Rosebank section of Staten Island, New York City, New York. It was home of Alice Austen, a photographer, for most of her lifetime, and is now a museum and a member of the Historic House Trust.
targets.riddle: Find 'Clear Comfort' in Rosebank, the historic trust museum that was home to one of America's first female photographers.

targets.name: Staten Island Children's Museum
targets.fact: A hands-on museum inside the grounds of Snug Harbor.
targets.about: The Staten Island Children's Museum is a children's museum on the grounds of Sailors' Snug Harbor on Staten Island, New York City. The museum opened in 1976 following community and government support for the project.
targets.riddle: Seek a hands-on place inside the grounds of Sailors' Snug Harbor, opened in 1976 following community and government support.

targets.name: Garibaldi-Meucci Museum
targets.fact: Home of Antonio Meucci, an early telephone inventor.
targets.riddle: Answer the call and find the home of an early telephone inventor.

targets.name: Staten Island Zoo
targets.fact: Famous for its large reptile collection and its groundhog, Chuck.
targets.about: The Staten Island Zoo is an 8-acre (3.2 ha) urban zoo in West New Brighton, Staten Island, New York City. The zoo is open year-round except on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day.
targets.riddle: Seek Chuck the groundhog and a large reptile collection at this 8-acre West New Brighton spot, closed on Christmas and Thanksgiving.

targets.name: Clove Lakes Park
targets.fact: Home to the oldest living thing in NYC, a 300-year-old tulip tree.
targets.about: Clove Lakes Park is a public park in the Sunnyside neighborhood of Staten Island in New York City. Clove Lakes Park has a rich natural history with valuable ecological assets and a few remnants of the past.
targets.riddle: In Sunnyside, Staten Island, find the oldest living thing in NYC, a 300-year-old tulip tree with remnants of the past.

targets.name: Von Briesen Park
targets.fact: A cliff-top park with a close view of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.
targets.riddle: Look out from this cliff-top for a close view of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.

targets.name: Richmond County Bank Ballpark
targets.fact: A ballpark with the Manhattan skyline behind the outfield.
targets.about: The Staten Island University Hospital Community Park (also SIUH Community Park; formerly the Richmond County Bank Ballpark) is a baseball stadium located on the northeastern tip of Staten Island in New York City.
targets.riddle: Head to the northeastern tip of Staten Island to find a baseball stadium with the Manhattan skyline behind the outfield.

targets.name: St. George Theatre
targets.fact: A 1929 movie palace with a Spanish-Baroque interior.
targets.about: The St. George Theatre is a performing arts venue, picture palace, and office complex at 35 Hyatt Street in St.
targets.riddle: Find a 1929 movie palace at 35 Hyatt with a Spanish-Baroque interior, performing arts, and an office complex.
